title: Help & Support
subtitle: Product help, usage guidance and support contact.

gettingStarted.title: Getting Started
gettingStarted.body: Sign in with the email and password your administrator set up for you. The first time (and whenever they change), you're shown what PROSM Time records about you and asked to acknowledge the Privacy Policy and Terms of Use. On the Dashboard, use Clock In to start your shift and Clock Out to end it - a live map shows your current position and, when relevant, the site's work area. The app opens in your device's language when it's one of the five supported; you can change it any time from the user menu. Employees open to their own home page: clock in and out, their hours today, this week (from Sunday) and this month, and links to their attendance record, allowances, timesheets and leave. The Owner, Managers and Supervisors open to the Dashboard. The Owner doesn't clock in or out.

attendance.title: Clocking In & Out
attendance.body: Choose your site (and project, if applicable) before clocking in - or leave Site empty and describe where you actually are if you're not at a registered location. Some sites require a photo, held steady for a moment so the app can confirm it's a live capture, not an old or static image. Right before anything is submitted, a confirmation screen shows exactly what's about to be recorded - your photo (if one was taken), your GPS location, the site/workplace and the time - with two optional fields, a note and your activity, which your manager can see. The time recorded is always the server's time, not your phone's clock. Clocking in is blocked on a day your approved leave covers. On the phone app, PROSM Time also reminds you itself - even when the app is closed: shortly after your shift's end if you're still clocked in, and a few minutes before your next scheduled shift.

walkInGeofence.title: Working at a Site You're Not Assigned To
walkInGeofence.body: If you're physically inside a registered site's work area today but aren't assigned there, it's suggested to you in the Site list (marked "you're here today"). Clocking in with no site at all still works too: your clock-in point becomes the centre of your organisation's no-site radius for the rest of that shift.

siteChange.title: Changing Sites Mid-Shift
siteChange.body: Change Site is its own button on the Dashboard whenever you're clocked in - no need to pause first. Pick where you've moved to (or leave Site empty), and the move is recorded with the time it happened. You're never clocked out in the process.

sos.title: SOS / Emergency
sos.body: The SOS button is on the Dashboard during every shift once your clock-in is confirmed. Pressing it sends a high-priority alert with your location to your site's managers, the Owner and co-workers clocked in at the same site, and it's logged in the Emergency Log. SOS is not an emergency service - it doesn't call the police or an ambulance. In an emergency, always call your local emergency number (in Egypt: ambulance 123, police 122, fire 180). It needs an internet connection. If you work without a chosen site, the managers of the nearest site receive it.

notifications.title: How Notifications Reach the Right Person
notifications.body: If you clock in or out - or move during your shift - outside your work area, you're asked to explain why, and the right person is notified: an employee's situation reaches that site's manager (and the Owner); a manager's own situation goes straight to the Owner. Tap a notification to jump to what it's about.

timesheets.title: Timesheets
timesheets.body: Once your manager generates a timesheet for a period, it appears under Timesheets for you to review and submit for approval. Worked time, breaks and overtime are shown as separate totals - break time is never subtracted from your worked hours, and overtime starts at the time your site's policy defines. Once approved, a timesheet is locked; if it needs a correction, request one from the timesheet's page.

exceptions.title: Reviews - Exceptions, Corrections, Offline Times and Fake Locations
exceptions.body: Everything that needs a manager's decision appears in the Manager Console under Pending Review: out-of-zone exceptions (with your reason), correction requests, actions recorded offline with the device's time, and locations reported as fake. If an exception is approved you're treated as present the full time. If it's rejected, your effective worked time is capped at the moment the situation was first detected. Flags are information for a person to review fairly - not automatic decisions.

allowances.title: Allowances
allowances.body: Open Allowances and pick a date to add an entry - the site and the day's times are filled in automatically: the first clock-in and the last clock-out of that day, and the details show how many sessions and hours you worked. Fill in meal, transportation, housing and other amounts, then Submit. A manager or the Owner approves or rejects it; while it's a draft you can still edit it.

kiosk.title: Kiosk Mode
kiosk.body: Open Kiosk Mode from the sidebar and pick a site to turn a shared tablet or computer into its clock-in screen for external workers (people without an app account - everyone with an account clocks in from the app). The worker types the 6-digit number the app made for them on the Workers page, then taps Clock in or Clock out; the screen returns to the keypad after each action. While the kiosk is open the device is locked to it: there's no menu, other pages and the back button lead back to the kiosk, and leaving needs the password of the account that opened it (the Exit kiosk button). Kiosk Mode is opened by the Owner, or by a Manager for a site they manage.

reportsCenter.title: Reports Center
reportsCenter.body: Pick a report type, a date range and, where relevant, an employee or site, then export it as a PDF. Reports include Attendance Record (offline device times are marked), Allowances, Workforce, Contractor, Site, Late Arrivals, Missed Checkouts, Leave Conflicts, Manager Overrides and Location Violations - which now lists being outside the work area (with the employee's reason and review status), implausible locations and fake locations together. A Manager sees only the sites they manage; the Owner sees the whole organisation. Next to every PDF download there is a Print button. In the PDF, a page never cuts through a row, the column headings repeat on each page and the pages are numbered.

sites.title: Sites (Administrators)
sites.body: Sites is where work sites are set up and people are assigned: name, address, GPS coordinates and radius, time zone, kiosk mode, and whether attendance, geofence or a photo are required. When you assign someone, their role at the site starts from their organisation role - a Manager or Supervisor becomes the site's manager, so they see its people. The rest of a site's behaviour is in Settings; the site form has an "Open this site's settings" link.

workers.title: External Workers
workers.body: Workers (in the sidebar, for the Owner and anyone who manages sites) is where you add people who work for you without an app account - contractors or day labour. Type the name (and the contractor, if any) and press Add: the app creates the worker's 6-digit number and shows it so you can copy it and give it to them. Workers belong to the whole organisation, not to one site: they clock in and out with their number at the kiosk of any site, and the list shows where each one is clocked in right now. You can force a clock-out (with a reason) if someone forgot, and deactivate a worker - a deactivated number stops working at the kiosk.

settingsCenter.title: Settings (Owner)
settingsCenter.body: Organisation-wide configuration: the no-site radius; "Reject clock-in/out from a fake location"; the defaults a new site starts from; and Site Policy - pick a site to change its GPS tolerance, grace period, shift hours, overtime and late-deduction timing, break rounding, ongoing presence monitoring, exempt employees, and the self-service blocks: after the grace period, clock-out outside the work area, and clock-in outside the work area.

leave.title: Leave (PTO)
leave.body: Request time off from the Leave page - pick a type (Annual, Sick, Unpaid, Emergency, Other), a date range and an optional reason (please don't include unnecessary health details). Only Annual leave tracks an entitled/used/remaining balance (21 days a year by default; the Owner can change an employee's entitlement from People). An employee's request goes to their site's manager (and the Owner); a manager's request goes to the Owner. Leave can't be approved over days that already have attendance. Approved leave counts toward your timesheet. Only the Owner and Managers approve leave: a Manager decides only for the people at the sites they manage, never for their own leave.

schedule.title: Shift Roster
schedule.body: See your own upcoming shifts on the Shift Roster page. Managers with scheduling authority can create shift templates per site and assign people to shifts, including overnight shifts (marked "(+1)"); overlapping shifts are refused automatically.

calendar.title: Hijri or Gregorian Calendar
calendar.body: Every date can show as Gregorian or Hijri - choose from the user menu, next to Language and Appearance. It's a per-device preference.

permissions.title: Permissions and Clocking On Behalf (Administrators)
permissions.body: Each person's page under People shows their permissions; whoever may change them can grant, revoke or reset one, with a reason. The Owner has every permission and can give any of them to anyone below. A Manager can give a Supervisor at their own sites a permission the Manager holds, and take it back. Approving leave and clocking someone in or out on their behalf are for the Owner and Managers only - never for oneself, and only for people below you at the sites you manage. Every change is recorded with who made it.

desktopApp.title: Windows Desktop App
desktopApp.body: The same PROSM Time as a Windows program. It opens filling your screen; F11 switches to fullscreen and Escape brings back the normal window. Your sign-in is remembered between launches.

liveMap.title: Live Map
liveMap.body: The Dashboard shows a map with your current position and, once you're clocked in or have a site selected, a circle marking that site's work area, so you can see where you stand before clocking in or out.

radio.title: Why There's a Radio in PROSM Time
radio.body: Play a station on your way to work, and PROSM Time is already open when you arrive - a small nudge against the most common attendance mistake: forgetting to clock in. It sends no personal data.

offline.title: Working Without Internet
offline.body: On your phone, Clock In, Clock Out, breaks and Change Site work with no connection; a small card tells you you're offline, and a bar shows how many actions are waiting. They're kept encrypted on the device and sent automatically, once, when the connection returns. Because these were recorded without the server, they keep your device's time: if it differs from the server's by more than 2 minutes, the action is marked "Device time (offline)" and your manager reviews it. A time earlier than your last recorded action, or on a day of approved leave, is refused - ask your manager to correct it. Other pages need a connection; if one can't load, the app tells you and lets you try again.

locationChecks.title: Work Areas and Fake Locations
locationChecks.body: Each site has a work area (a circle on the map). Clocking in or out outside it is recorded as an exception and you're asked why; one reason covers the whole trip, even if both your clock-out and your next clock-in were outside. A site can also be set to refuse a self clock-in from outside its area - then ask your manager to clock you in. On Android, PROSM Time notices when the location comes from a mock-location (fake GPS) app: it's recorded and reviewed by your manager, and your organisation may choose to refuse it. Faking your location or your phone's time is against the Terms of Use.

privacy.title: Your Privacy
privacy.body: PROSM Time records your location when you clock in or out, take a break, change site or send an SOS. Only if your organisation turns on presence monitoring is it also recorded about every 5 minutes during your shift - on Android also in the background, after telling you first and with a visible notification - and it always stops when you clock out. A photo is taken only where your site requires one; there's no facial recognition. Your organisation's managers see your records. Location samples are deleted after 30 days and photos after 90 days. You can withdraw location or camera permission in your device settings at any time. For your rights over your data, ask your organisation first, or write to info@prosm.net. Full details are in the Privacy Policy and Terms of Use below.

q1.question: I forgot to clock out - what do I do?
q1.answer: Contact an administrator or manager - they can record the correct Clock Out on your behalf, and the action is recorded as theirs, not yours. A manager can also submit a correction request on an already-recorded time, which - once approved - genuinely updates it.

q2.question: Why was my Clock In flagged as outside my work area?
q2.answer: Your site has a configured geofence and GPS accuracy tolerance (or, with no site selected, your organization's own no-site radius around where you clocked in). If your reported location fell outside that area, you're asked to explain why so the right manager can review it - approving it clears the flag entirely; rejecting it caps your worked time at that moment.

q3.question: Which time is recorded when I clock in?
q3.answer: The server's time, always - changing your phone's clock has no effect. The only exception is an action made without a connection: it keeps the device's time, and if that differs from the server's by more than 2 minutes, it's marked for your manager to review.

q4.question: How do I change the language or theme?
q4.answer: Open the user menu (bottom of the sidebar) - Language and Appearance (Dark/Light/System) can be changed there at any time, and you can also set your profile picture from the same menu.

q5.question: I clocked in without choosing a site - why did it ask for a "workplace"?
q5.answer: Site is optional so you can register attendance from your real current location even when it isn't a registered site - but a short description of where you actually are is required in that case, so reports never show a blank site. Your organization's own no-site radius still protects that session the same way a real site's geofence would.

q6.question: What's the difference between Attendance Record and Timesheets?
q6.answer: Attendance Record is a live, date-ranged log of clock-in/out events - nothing to approve. Timesheets are a generated, period-based object (worked/break/overtime totals) that goes through a real submit -> approve workflow and gets locked once approved.

q7.question: Can I export my attendance or timesheet as a PDF?
q7.answer: Yes - Attendance Record, Timesheets and Allowances each have their own Export PDF action, scoped to whatever you're currently viewing, and Reports gathers the Attendance Record and Allowances exports in one dedicated place too. Each also has a Print button, and your home page links to all of them.

q8.question: Why can't I see some employees in People or Attendance Record?
q8.answer: You only ever see yourself, plus - if you manage a site - the people assigned to that site. The Owner sees everyone. This is enforced by the server, not just hidden in the interface.

q9.question: Does the desktop app sign me out every time I close it?
q9.answer: No - your session is remembered between launches, the same way it is on your phone or in a browser.

q10.question: Can I still play the radio while I'm clocked in?
q10.answer: Yes - it keeps playing in the background regardless of your attendance status. It lives in the sidebar's Media row (tap it to expand the station list and search) rather than the header, and takes up very little space when collapsed.

q11.question: How does the 30-day demo work?
q11.answer: On the Welcome page, Use the demo version opens the usual activation without the activation code; your organisation and owner are created at once. The trial lasts 30 days (server time) and a bar shows the days left. A week before the end the owner gets a notice and an email with sales@prosm.net, info@prosm.net and support@prosm.net. When it ends, the app pauses and nothing is deleted: enter a purchased activation code on the page that appears, or ask PROSM to renew the license - then everything continues with all your data. One trial per email.

q12.question: Does attendance work without internet?
q12.answer: Yes. On your phone, Clock In, Clock Out, breaks and Change Site work with no connection, with the photo and location taken at that moment. They're kept encrypted on the device, in order, and sent automatically once when the connection returns - never twice. Times that differ from the server's are marked for review. Other pages need a connection.

q13.question: Why does my record say "Device time (offline)"?
q13.answer: That action was made without a connection and recorded with your phone's time, which differed from the server's by more than 2 minutes. Your manager sees it in Pending Review and can approve it or correct it.

q14.question: Who can see my location and photos, and for how long?
q14.answer: You, your site's managers and your organisation's Owner. Location samples taken during a shift are deleted after 30 days and attendance photos after 90 days. The Privacy Policy explains the rest.

q15.question: Does SOS call the ambulance or the police?
q15.answer: No. It alerts your site's managers, the Owner and co-workers on site, with your location. In an emergency, call your local emergency number yourself (in Egypt: ambulance 123, police 122, fire 180).
